solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dull article: give notice to superannuated poet

parts.note: mat, a variant spelling of matt, means dull and without shine
the definite article
to warn is to give notice of something
superannuated means old, retired through age

explanation.surface: A tedious piece of writing serves notice of retirement on an elderly versifier.
explanation.walkthrough: The four pieces run straight through both lights: MAT, THE, WARN, OLD; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian writer of Dover Beach was a celebrated English poet and critic.

clue.text: I hope you stay as you are forever while in the sun

definitions.text: I hope you stay as you are forever while in the sun

parts.words: I hope you stay as you are forever while in the sun
parts.note: a traditional Eastern blessing wishing someone lasting prosperity, read whimsically as a wish that the figure cast by your body in sunlight never shrinks

explanation.surface: A heartfelt wish that a friend never changes, offered on a sunny day.
explanation.definitionFit: The Persian-origin greeting wishes undiminished fortune, literally that one's silhouette in the sun keep its size.

clue.text: Beaten 1-0, Trust turns to traveller

indicators.note: something beaten is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the figures read as the letters I and O

explanation.surface: A football club called Trust loses by a single goal on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the score 1-0 as the letters I and O, add TRUST and rearrange; 'turns to' is the link meaning 'becomes'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist is a sightseer, someone travelling for pleasure.

clue.text: Bisexual philosopher?

parts.note: both sexes: a male pronoun followed by a girl in upper-class pronunciation
both sexes: a male pronoun followed by a girl in upper-class pronunciation

explanation.surface: A question about a thinker's love life.
explanation.walkthrough: GEL is the plummy British way of saying 'girl'; HE plus GEL covers both sexes.
explanation.definitionFit: The German idealist thinker of the dialectic is one of philosophy's great names.

clue.text: Leave having achieved parity?

parts.note: with means having, as in a man with a hat
a draw is a result where the sides end level

explanation.surface: A team walks off the field after equalising.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw is to pull out or depart, a synonym of leaving.

clue.text: See 1
Marina wrong element for him?

indicators.note: wrong signals the letters of the word marina set out in a different order

explanation.surface: A harbour is not the natural setting for this person.
explanation.walkthrough: A marina is a place of water, the wrong element for a flier, whose element is the air, so the whole clue defines as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A flier in an air force lives in the air, not the sea of a harbour.

clue.text: Polaris needs transport using hydrogen for power

indicators.note: needs here hints the word must be reworked, its letters shuffled into a new order
using one thing in place of another marks a substitution
for marks what is replaced: hydrogen stands in for power

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A nuclear missile system requires fuel-powered vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: In TRANSPORT replace P with H to get TRANSHORT, whose letters rearranged give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris is the name of the star almost directly above the earth's pole, used for navigation.

clue.text: Walker obtains colleague without offence

parts.note: a leg is what one walks with
an ally is a partner or associate

explanation.surface: A hiker joins up with a workmate in all innocence.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting within the law means committing no offence.

clue.text: Child solvers' grasping gents' solution

indicators.note: grasping means holding, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: belonging to you, the solvers: your

indicators.note: a solution dissolves and remixes, signalling the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A youngster in a crossword club holds the gents' answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solution' looks like the crossword's answer but signals the anagram; 'grasping' has the solvers' word hold NGSTE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A youngster is a young person, a child.

clue.text: King's daughter, say, hurried round

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: ran means hurried
e.g., for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: A princess rushes about.
explanation.walkthrough: The king is Shakespeare's Lear, whose daughters are Goneril, Regan and Cordelia.
explanation.definitionFit: In King Lear, the monarch's second daughter is one of the two who betray him.

clue.text: See 1
Window, one in Russian city

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the city's name

parts.note: Orel is a city south of Moscow
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A window display in a Russian town.
explanation.definitionFit: An oriel is a bay window projecting from an upper storey.

clue.text: Ballet master arranging vigil with head

indicators.note: arranging sets letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A dance teacher organises an overnight watch with a headteacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergei Diaghilev founded the Ballets Russes, the great impresario of ballet.

clue.text: Playwright of unusual art, maybe giant

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters of art set out differently
maybe suggests an alternative arrangement of giant's letters

explanation.surface: A dramatist known for strange work, perhaps on a huge scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' turns ART into RAT and 'maybe' turns GIANT into TIGAN; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence Rattigan wrote The Browning Version and The Winslow Boy for the stage.

clue.text: Transitional speculation, not great, in pub

indicators.note: in places the wager and the small word inside the pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
a bet is a speculation
wee means small, not great

explanation.surface: A small wager placed in a pub in a time of change.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in between sits at an intermediate, transitional stage.

clue.text: Canonised philosopher should last the course

parts.note: ST abbreviates saint, one canonised
A. J. Ayer was a British logical positivist philosopher

explanation.surface: A sainted thinker is expected to go the distance.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a verb phrase but describes a racehorse that can last the course.
explanation.definitionFit: In racing, a horse with stamina for long distances is called this, one that endures.

clue.text: Rogue knight sounds like bogus Welshman

indicators.note: sounds like says the words are heard rather than written

parts.note: false means bogus; Taff is a slang name for a Welshman

explanation.surface: A roguish knight seems to be a fake from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Taff (from the River Taff, or Dafydd) is British slang for a Welshman.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Falstaff is Shakespeare's fat, dishonest knight.

clue.text: Confederate in call for attention because of this

indicators.note: in places the soldier inside the call

parts.note: hey is a call to catch someone's attention
a Reb was a Confederate soldier in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: A Southern rebel calls out, giving a reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereby is a formal word meaning by this means, as a result of this.

clue.text: Get back into position with purge or otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, here another letter order

explanation.surface: A party rebuilds itself after a purge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops regroup when they reassemble in formation after disruption.

clue.text: Spaniard who works like a dog?

definitions.meaning: in Spanish the word means a farm labourer, a working man
a retriever breed originally from Newfoundland

explanation.surface: A hardworking man from Spain toils endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like a' links the two senses; the question mark flags the Spanish meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The retriever breed's name is the Spanish word for a labourer.

clue.text: Creatures about 100 holes ahead and to play?

indicators.note: about means around, so the golfing term surrounds the numeral

parts.note: in golf, dormie describes a player as many holes up as remain to be played
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A puzzle about animals, a hundred holes and a game.
explanation.walkthrough: DORMIE is a golf term: a player is dormie when leading by as many holes as are left, so cannot lose.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormice are small hibernating rodents, woodland creatures.

clue.text: Needing a leg-up due to large scale affliction

indicators.note: needing here suggests the letters require reworking into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone requires a boost because of a widespread disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'due to' is a link; the letters of A LEG-UP rearranged give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A plague is an epidemic, a disease or calamity spreading widely.

clue.text: Heart drug: this in, analogue is out

definitions.meaning: a medicine from foxglove used to treat heart conditions
a cryptic sense: the opposite of analogue is in fashion, said as a short sentence

explanation.surface: A cardiac medicine for the new technology age.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as two words: 'digital is (in)', the opposite of analogue.
explanation.definitionFit: The foxglove extract strengthens heart contractions and is a classic cardiac medicine.

clue.text: Former display includes royal insect eater

indicators.note: includes means contains, so one piece sits inside

parts.note: shew is an old spelling of show

explanation.surface: An old show has a regal insect-eating animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The shrew is a small mammal that feeds largely on insects.

clue.text: Back to the grave?

definitions.meaning: the rear part of a ship

explanation.surface: A question about returning to the cemetery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the' is a link joining the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear of a boat bears this name, and so does a severe, serious look.

clue.text: Complete with part of course

parts.note: a golf course is divided into holes

explanation.surface: Something is full with a section of the course.
explanation.definitionFit: Whole means entire, complete.

clue.text: Source of juicy rumours?

parts.note: juicy plays on a fruit-bearing plant and on scandalous gossip passed along informally

explanation.surface: Where gossip comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearing something through the informal network of gossip, and literally the plant bearing juicy fruit.

clue.text: Smell successive notes among vocalists that go well with fools

indicators.note: among places the smell and notes inside the singers

parts.note: singers are vocalists
pong is British slang for a bad smell
E and F are adjacent notes in the musical scale

explanation.surface: An odour drifts among a choir as consecutive notes are sung.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool here is a British dessert of fruit puree and cream, often served with these biscuits.
explanation.definitionFit: These light finger-shaped biscuits are served alongside creamy fruit desserts.
